entries.title: I Samuel 3:1
segments:
Precious; rare, uncommon. 
 
  No open vision; literally, "vision was not spread abroad," that is, revelations from God were not common. 
 
Those who are blessed with a fulness of divine instruction and with all the means of grace, but very faintly realize the sad condition of such as are without them, wandering in darkness and the shadow of death.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:2
segments: Eyesight is a great blessing, which should be carefully preserved and wisely employed; that in case of its loss, the mind, in rich stores of knowledge, may have materials for useful and happy contemplation.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:5
segments: Cheerful readiness in children to comply with the wishes of parents and teachers, in an indication of great excellence of character, and of eminent usefulness in future life.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:7
segments:
Did not yet know the Lord; did not know him in the way of receiving revelations from him. 
 
God by his Spirit, in his word and his providence, sometimes repeatedly speaks to men before they are aware of it, especially if they are young and have not been accustomed to distinguish his voice from that of others.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:10
segments: When men, and even children, manifest a readiness to be instructed by God, he will communicate to them a knowledge of his will; and though it may be trying, yet in doing it they will be accepted of him and receive a great reward.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:13
segments: Parents, to please God and escape his indignation, must not only pray with and for their children, and counsel and advise them, but must also govern them; and if they are disposed to be openly vicious, must inflict such punishment as will effectually restrain them.  Nor must fear or favor hinder them from exercising the authority and power which God has given them for this purpose.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:14
segments: Not be purged; not so done away as to prevent the threatened punishment.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:17
segments:
Do so to thee; punish thee. 
 
Parents should encourage their children freely and fully to communicate with them on all things in which they are interested, especially on the subject of religion and whatever pertains to the performance of duty.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:18
segments: When the will of God is made known, true piety in vigorous exercise will lead the soul to acquiesce in it, feeling that what God says must be true, and what he does must be right and good.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:19
segments:
Let none of his words fall; let none of his predictions fail of their accomplishment. 
 
When men follow the directions of God so far as they know them, he will communicate to them an increasing knowledge of his will, and by experience they will acquire the habit of readily understanding and promptly obeying it.

entries.title: I Samuel 3:20
segments: From Dan even to Beer-sheba; from one end of the land to the other.
